meta.description: Tagging taxonomy for the WCT GLP-1 study. Segment annotations in segment_tags.json draw their theme, subtheme, emotion, sentiment, and semantic values from this codebook. Editable and versioned; bump schema_version when tags are added or revised.
changelog: 1.0 — initial themes, emotions, sentiment scale, semantic tags.
1.1 — added subthemes to 10 themes with internal nuance.
1.2 — added subthemes to drug_switching, side_effect_concern, injection_experience, education_need, and weight_loss_history after reviewing participant_10.
notes: A segment may carry a theme with no subtheme (general use) or with one or more subthemes.
A subtheme may only be applied if its parent theme is also applied to the segment.
Flat themes (no subthemes) have no `subthemes` key.

theme_tags.description: Affordability and out-of-pocket cost of medication or participation.

subthemes.description: Paying for medication or care out of pocket.
Changes in medication price or affordability over time.

theme_tags.description: Insurance coverage, prior authorization, or pharmacy benefit manager obstacles.
Availability of the drug: shortages, lawsuits, supply, getting hold of it.
Worry about adverse effects or health complications from the medication.

subthemes.description: Gastrointestinal or gastric-emptying side effects.
A major health complication that would force stopping treatment.
Concern about unknown side effects or being among the first to try a treatment.

theme_tags.description: Health improvements beyond weight loss.

subthemes.description: Blood pressure, cholesterol, or other cardiometabolic improvement.
Reduced heartburn, reflux, or other digestive improvement.
Reduction in food noise or intrusive appetite-related thoughts.
Improvement in sleep, stress, mood, or energy.

theme_tags.description: Concern about regaining weight if treatment stops or a placebo is received.
Intent to stay on medication, lifelong use, or maintenance commitment.
Willingness to switch to or try a different medication.

subthemes.description: Switching or adding medication to break a weight-loss stall or plateau.

theme_tags.description: Feelings about placebo arms, randomization, or controlled-study design.
Attitudes toward injections: frequency, dislike, route of administration.

subthemes.description: Injection cadence — weekly versus monthly dosing.
Dislike of or discomfort with the act of injecting.
Concern about how long a dose lasts between injections.

theme_tags.description: Interest in or preference for oral / pill-form GLP-1 medications.
Use of or views on compounded medication versus brand-name product.
Factors that attract the participant to joining a clinical trial.

subthemes.description: Joining a trial primarily to gain access to medication.
Attraction driven by convenient or local trial logistics.

theme_tags.description: Contributing to science, helping others, or supporting research as a motivation.
Distance and travel required to reach trial or clinic sites.

subthemes.description: Distance and driving time required to reach a site.
Having, or lacking, a means of transport.

theme_tags.description: Time cost of participation: hours per week, round trips, scheduling load.
Visit frequency, home visits, telehealth, and scheduling arrangements.

subthemes.description: Remote or telehealth visits in place of in-person ones.
A nurse or staff member visiting the participant's home.
How often site visits are required.
Appointment scheduling and flexibility.
Preference for a nearby or locally managed site.

theme_tags.description: Trial procedures such as fasting blood draws or continuous glucose monitoring.

subthemes.description: Fasting blood draws.
Continuous glucose monitoring.

theme_tags.description: Vouchers, financial compensation, travel concierge, devices, or other support offered.

subthemes.description: Direct payment for participation.
Vouchers for medication, books, or weight-loss products.
Arranged travel or transport to sites.
Provision of a device such as a Fitbit or tracker.
Meal replacement drinks or meal vouchers.
Continued access to medication after the trial.

theme_tags.description: Desire for nutrition, lifestyle, or medication education and its formats.

subthemes.description: Nutritional counseling, meal planning, recipes.
Format of education — videos, webinars, modules, classes, handouts.
Education about the medication itself and how to take it.
Journaling or self-tracking of mood, food, or progress.

theme_tags.description: Past weight-loss attempts, diets, and the participant's weight journey.

subthemes.description: Past dieting approaches such as Atkins, paleo, vegan, or commercial programs.
Earlier weight-loss medications tried before GLP-1s (e.g. phentermine).
Bariatric or weight-loss surgery, considered or undergone.
Past experience with or difficulty sustaining exercise.
A long-running or lifelong struggle with weight, including weight cycling.

theme_tags.description: Awareness of clinical trials or new drugs in development.

emotion_tags.description: Worry, unease, or apprehension about an outcome.
Relief, reassurance, or being put at ease.
Self-assurance or certainty in a decision or knowledge.
Excitement, eagerness, or strong positive interest.
Doubt about claims, value, or trustworthiness.
Interest in learning more or exploring an option.

semantic_tags.description: Reasoning about how to obtain or retain access to medication.
Weighing risks, side effects, or trial-design probabilities.
Framing the medication as needed or relied upon long-term.
Reasoning about sustaining weight loss after the active treatment phase.
Trading effort or burden against convenience or accessibility.
Practical obstacles that make trial participation harder.
The participant or their clinician actively pushing to get care.
Actively seeking knowledge, education, or trial information.
Narrative of meaningful health improvement or change.
Justifying a choice by benefit to others or to science.
A decision framed as contingent on specific conditions ('it depends').
Reasoning about diet, exercise, or behavior change alongside medication.
